WEEKS.title: Setup
WEEKS.intent: Two or three hours. Half the frustration in month one is environment problems, not concept problems.
build: Sign up for the Power Apps Developer Plan — free, full Dataverse sandbox for all 24 weeks
Create DEV, TEST and PROD environments if your tenant allows it
Sign in to Microsoft Learn so module progress tracks
Set up a notes repo — OneNote, Obsidian or GitHub
Pick your spine project and name it
Book PL-900 for Week 5
WEEKS.ai: Nothing yet. Get the environments standing up first.
WEEKS.checkpoint: Environments live, PL-900 booked, spine project named.
WEEKS.note: Do not start the Copilot Studio or Power Pages trials yet. They are timed — Week 17 and Week 20.

WEEKS.title: Platform orientation & environments
WEEKS.intent: Get oriented, and turn a vague ambition into a written brief you can build against.
learn: PL-900 paths: business value and core components
Skim the PL-900T00-A course outline as your four-week roadmap
watch: April Dunnam — Power Platform overview (2026 content only)
Microsoft Power Platform official channel — current platform tour
build: Create your DEV environment; note its type, region and Dataverse status
Explore the Maker Portal, Admin Center and platform analytics
List ten manual processes at your work this platform could solve — pick your spine project from them
WEEKS.ai: Have an AI assistant play requirements analyst and ask you ten clarifying questions about your spine project. Answer them. That transcript is your brief.
WEEKS.checkpoint: One-page project brief: scope, users, and the top five things it must do.

WEEKS.title: Dataverse: tables, columns, relationships
WEEKS.intent: Model the data before you build anything pretty. This is the decision you live with for years.
learn: Get started with Microsoft Dataverse
Create tables in Dataverse
watch: Shane Young — Dataverse table basics
Lisa Crosbie — Dataverse for beginners
build: Model your tables on paper first — entities, keys, cardinality — before touching the maker portal
Build 5–7 tables with correct column types (choice vs lookup vs text is the one you'll regret)
Create 1:N and N:N relationships; understand cascade behaviour on delete
Load 50+ rows of realistic sample data
WEEKS.ai: Paste your schema into an AI assistant and ask it to critique it specifically as a Dataverse model — normalisation, choice vs lookup, relationship limits. Then have it generate 100 rows of realistic CSV for your domain and import them.
WEEKS.checkpoint: An ERD you drew, plus a working schema with sample data in it.

WEEKS.title: Dataverse logic: keys, business rules, rollups
WEEKS.intent: Learn where business logic belongs. Most people put it in the wrong layer for years.
learn: Dataverse business logic: business rules, calculated columns, rollup columns, alternate keys
watch: Search: Dataverse business rules
Search: Dataverse rollup columns — Shane Young, Andrew Hess
build: Add calculated columns (days open, total cost)
Add a rollup column and learn its 12-hour recalculation lag the easy way
Write three business rules — visibility, required, default value
Build four custom views with real filtering and sorting
Set up alternate keys for integration-safe upserts
WEEKS.ai: Describe a rule in plain English and ask whether it belongs in a business rule, calculated column, real-time workflow or cloud flow — and why. Verify against docs; AI misses Dataverse edge cases fairly often.
WEEKS.checkpoint: A 300-word explainer: business rule vs calculated column vs flow. AB-410 topic and a real interview question.

WEEKS.title: Security model
WEEKS.intent: The topic separating people who can build a demo from people who can deploy to an enterprise.
learn: Dataverse security: business units, roles, teams, column-level security, hierarchy security, sharing
watch: Search: Dataverse security roles explained (2025–2026 only — business unit behaviour changed)
build: Create three roles: Requester, Fulfiller, Manager
Set privilege depth correctly for each — User / BU / Parent-Child / Organization
Apply column-level security to one sensitive field
Create a second user account and actually log in as them to test
WEEKS.ai: Have AI quiz you on PL-900 objectives — 25 scenario questions cold, then explanations for every miss, then five harder ones on your weakest domain.
WEEKS.checkpoint: Security matrix documented (role × table × privilege), verified by real login testing.

WEEKS.title: PL-900 exam week
WEEKS.intent: Sit the exam. Then map the rest of the plan against the AB-410 objectives.
learn: Official PL-900 practice assessment on the Microsoft Learn credential page
Read the AB-410 study guide end to end — to map, not to study
build: Light review Monday to Wednesday
Sit PL-900 Thursday or Friday
Annotate every AB-410 objective with the week that covers it
WEEKS.ai: Ask AI to turn the AB-410 study guide into a checklist of discrete, testable skills. That checklist is your Week 16 self-assessment.
WEEKS.checkpoint: PL-900 passed. Annotated AB-410 objective map.

WEEKS.title: Model-driven apps
WEEKS.intent: Model-driven first, deliberately. It forces you to work with the data model rather than around it.
learn: Create a model-driven app with Dataverse
Optional: PL-7003 Applied Skill — model-driven apps
watch: Lisa Crosbie — model-driven app series (strong on the why, not just the click path)
build: Full model-driven app for your spine project's back office
Main form with tabs, sections and a proper header
Quick create form and quick view form
Sub-grids showing related records
Sitemap with sensible areas, groups and subareas
Custom view plus a chart on the main table
WEEKS.ai: Ask AI to review your form design for data-entry usability — field grouping, tab order, cognitive load. Implement two suggestions.
WEEKS.checkpoint: An app someone else could navigate without you explaining it.

WEEKS.title: Business process flows
WEEKS.intent: BPFs and business rules are old and unglamorous, and they carry real weight on AB-410.
learn: Business process flows, form-level business rules, embedded canvas apps
watch: Search: business process flows Power Platform — cover the maker experience and the tables BPFs create
build: A BPF for your request lifecycle with stage-gating conditions
Form-level business rules that show and hide by stage
One embedded canvas app on a form
An editable grid on a sub-grid
WEEKS.ai: Ask AI to explain the table a BPF generates in Dataverse and why that matters for reporting and security. Verify against docs.
WEEKS.checkpoint: Working BPF with stage-gated required fields, plus a written note on what it creates behind the scenes.

WEEKS.title: Canvas apps & Power Fx
WEEKS.intent: Delegation is the number one real-world canvas app failure and the thing juniors never check.
learn: Create a canvas app in Power Apps
Power Fx formula reference
Optional: PL-7001 Applied Skill — canvas apps
watch: Reza Dorrani — canvas fundamentals and Power Fx
Shane Young — same ground, slower pace
build: Canvas app on your Dataverse tables
Gallery with search, sort and filter using delegable functions
Form with SubmitForm, Patch, validation and error handling
Set vs UpdateContext vs collections — know when each is correct
Navigation across four or more screens
WEEKS.ai: Feed your Power Fx to AI for delegation and performance review — but verify every suggestion. Models routinely invent Power Fx functions that don't exist or confuse it with Excel.
WEEKS.checkpoint: Zero delegation warnings against a 2,000+ row table.

WEEKS.title: Responsive design, components, performance
WEEKS.intent: Rebuild it properly. Containers, reusable components, and a load time you'd accept yourself.
learn: Canvas components, responsive layouts, performance optimisation
watch: Reza Dorrani — responsive design and reusable components
Search: Power Apps performance optimization
build: Rebuild responsive — containers, no absolute positioning
Two reusable components with custom input and output properties
A component library, consumed by your app
Optimise: concurrent loading, less OnStart work, App.StartScreen, fewer controls
Device features: camera, barcode scanner, GPS
WEEKS.ai: Have AI generate a Power Fx theme object — colours, spacing, type scale — and apply it globally. Tedious, well-specified, easily verified. Good AI work.
WEEKS.checkpoint: Loads in under 3 seconds and works on your actual phone.

WEEKS.title: Connectors & integration
WEEKS.intent: Connection references matter now because Week 24's ALM work depends on them.
learn: Connectors and data sources
Introduction to custom connectors
watch: Search: Power Apps custom connector — Reza Dorrani, Damien Bird
build: Connect to SharePoint and Office 365 Users
Build one custom connector against a public REST API
Understand connection references properly
Write down your answer to: when should data live in SharePoint vs Dataverse?
WEEKS.ai: Give AI an OpenAPI spec, have it explain each operation and draft the connector definition. Import and test it.
WEEKS.checkpoint: A working custom connector used in both an app and a flow.

WEEKS.title: Real users
WEEKS.intent: No new material. This is the week a study project becomes a work project.
build: Put the app in front of two or three actual colleagues
Watch them use it without helping — do not explain, do not defend
Fix the top five problems they hit
Write a short user guide
WEEKS.ai: Feed your observation notes to AI and ask it to sort the issues into UX, data model and training problems. The sorting is the point — each needs a different fix.
WEEKS.checkpoint: Three real users have used it. Bug list written, top five fixed.
WEEKS.note: Slack week. If you're behind, this is where you catch up.

WEEKS.title: Cloud flows: triggers, actions, expressions
WEEKS.intent: Trigger conditions and filtering attributes. Skip them and you will build an infinite loop — everyone does this once.
learn: Create flows in Power Automate
Optional: PL-7002 Applied Skill — automated processes
watch: Damien Bird and Reza Dorrani — both exceptional here
Search: Power Automate triggers explained / expressions
build: Automated flow on row create/update using filtering attributes and trigger conditions
Instant flow triggered from your canvas app
Scheduled flow for a weekly digest
Master: formatDateTime, addDays, if, coalesce, outputs, body, first, length
Parse JSON from an HTTP action
WEEKS.ai: Describe a transformation in plain English, get the expression. Genuinely strong AI use case — expression syntax is fiddly. Still test every one.
WEEKS.checkpoint: Four working flows, including one whose trigger condition correctly prevents self-triggering.

WEEKS.title: Approvals & error handling
WEEKS.intent: Flows that survive contact with reality. Resilience thinking is a seniority marker rarely taught in tutorials.
learn: Approvals, error handling patterns, scope and run-after configuration
watch: Search: Power Automate error handling try catch
Search: Power Automate approvals advanced
build: Multi-stage approval routing with a threshold branch
Try / Catch / Finally using Scopes with configured run-after
Retry policies and a terminate action with a meaningful message
Adaptive card approval posted to Teams
SLA escalation: unapproved after three business days, escalate
WEEKS.ai: Give AI a flow with no error handling and ask it to design a resilience strategy — what retries, what fails loudly, what degrades gracefully. Implement it.
WEEKS.checkpoint: A flow that fails gracefully and tells someone useful. Break it deliberately and confirm.

WEEKS.title: Child flows, HTTP, desktop flows
WEEKS.intent: PL-500 retired but desktop flows are alive. Learn them because your workplace has legacy systems, not for a badge.
learn: Child flows, solution-aware flows, Power Automate Desktop basics
watch: Damien Bird — child flows and reusable patterns
Search: Power Automate Desktop tutorial 2026
build: A child flow for a reusable operation, called from three parents
Direct Dataverse Web API calls via HTTP with Azure AD auth
One desktop flow automating a genuinely legacy task
Apply to each with concurrency tuning — and know when concurrency breaks your logic
WEEKS.ai: Ask AI to review your flow architecture for coupling: which flows break if the data model changes? Refactor the worst one.
WEEKS.checkpoint: A child flow consumed by three parents, and a working desktop flow.

WEEKS.title: Business logic architecture
WEEKS.intent: Where does each piece of logic belong? Most consultants can't answer this in writing. You will.
learn: Dataverse plug-ins (conceptual), real-time vs background workflows, the full decision framework
watch: Search: Dataverse plugins vs flows — you want the architectural decision, not the C#
build: Document a decision tree: for every piece of logic in your solution, which layer and why
Refactor two pieces you put in the wrong place back in Phase 1
WEEKS.ai: Present three scenarios and ask for recommendations with tradeoffs — latency, transaction scope, licensing, maintainability. Argue back where you disagree. The disagreement is the exercise.
WEEKS.checkpoint: A written business logic decision matrix. Genuinely SME-level output.

WEEKS.title: Buffer & consolidation
WEEKS.intent: Deliberate slack. If you're on schedule, bank credentials. If you're behind, you're now caught up.
build: Rebuild your weakest Phase 2 component with what you know now
Sit the free PL-7001, PL-7002 and PL-7003 Applied Skills assessments
Score yourself 1–5 against every AB-410 objective
WEEKS.ai: Have AI generate a 40-question mixed practice set from the AB-410 study guide, weighted toward your low scores.
WEEKS.checkpoint: Honest self-assessment against every AB-410 objective.

WEEKS.title: Power Pages foundations
WEEKS.intent: The product most people skip — which is exactly why knowing it well pays.
WEEKS.trial: Start your Power Pages trial now (30 days, renewable).
learn: Get started with Power Pages
Demonstrate the capabilities of Microsoft Power Pages
watch: Dhruvin Shah — the most complete Power Pages content on YouTube
Search: Power Pages tutorial 2026
build: Provision a site from a template
Design Studio: pages, sections, navigation, styling, theming
Basic forms and lists bound to your Dataverse tables
Publish, then view it as an anonymous user
WEEKS.ai: Ask AI to draft the information architecture for your portal — what an external submitter sees, in what order, with what expectations set at each step.
WEEKS.checkpoint: A published site rendering live Dataverse data.

WEEKS.title: Portal security & table permissions
WEEKS.intent: The week that matters. Portal security is where organisations get hurt.
learn: Work with Power Pages websites — authentication, table permissions, web roles
build: Configure authentication plus at least one external identity provider
Table permissions: Global, Contact, Account, Parent, Self — know each precisely
Web roles and page permissions
Multistep forms with save-and-resume
Log in as user A and try to reach user B's record by editing the URL. It must fail.
WEEKS.ai: Describe your table permission config and ask AI to find data exposure risks — then verify each manually. Don't outsource the conclusion; a confident wrong answer here is expensive.
WEEKS.checkpoint: A written security test log: 8+ access scenarios, expected result, actual result.

WEEKS.title: Liquid, Web API, custom code
WEEKS.intent: Turn a content site into a real web application.
learn: Extend Power Pages — Liquid, Web API, ALM
watch: Dhruvin Shah — Liquid templates and Portal Web API in depth
build: Liquid templates rendering Dataverse data — fetchxml, entitylist, entityview
Portal Web API calls for client-side create and update
Custom JavaScript form validation
A Power Automate flow triggered by a portal submission
Custom CSS matched to your organisation's brand
WEEKS.ai: Have AI generate Liquid for a specific rendering need, then explain the security implications of every tag used. Liquid can expose data if used carelessly.
WEEKS.checkpoint: External submission writes to Dataverse, triggers a flow, notifies your team. End to end.

WEEKS.title: Copilot Studio foundations
WEEKS.intent: The centre of gravity of the platform in 2026. Treat these four weeks as the most career-relevant here.
WEEKS.trial: Start your Copilot Studio trial now (60 days).
learn: Copilot Studio fundamentals: agents, topics, knowledge sources, actions
AI Builder and AI Hub: prompts, models, prebuilt models — AB-410 objectives
watch: Nick DeCourcy (Bright Ideas Agency) — Copilot Studio depth
Daniel Christian — focused agent tutorials
Lisa Crosbie — Copilot inside apps
build: An agent for your spine project with five or more authored topics
Knowledge sources: a SharePoint site, a public URL, uploaded documents
Actions calling your existing Power Automate flows
Generative answers with scoped, well-written instructions
Publish to Teams and test with a real colleague
WEEKS.ai: Iterate the agent's instructions with AI: draft, test against ten real user questions, feed failures back, revise. Prompt engineering is an AB-620 measured skill and this is how you learn it.
WEEKS.checkpoint: A published agent answering real questions about your data.

WEEKS.title: AB-410 exam week
WEEKS.intent: Broad exam. Expect scenario clusters and more weight on BPFs and business rules than you'd guess.
learn: AB-410 study guide, three domains — target your lowest Week 16 scores
build: Focused review Monday to Wednesday
Sit AB-410 Thursday or Friday
WEEKS.ai: Have AI drill you on scenario questions in the exam's style — multi-part, linked to a single business situation, rather than isolated facts.
WEEKS.checkpoint: AB-410 passed.
WEEKS.note: Microsoft Learn is available inside the exam. Safety net, not a strategy. Retakes allowed after 24 hours, but use the score report to rebuild first.

WEEKS.title: MCP, multi-agent, Foundry
WEEKS.intent: AB-620 territory and the genuine frontier of the platform.
learn: AB-620 study guide: plan and configure, integrate and extend, test and manage
build: Connect your agent to an MCP server as a tool source
Build a second specialist agent and configure agent-to-agent handoff
Custom connectors and API actions as agent tools
Adaptive cards for structured responses
A custom prompt from the Microsoft Foundry model catalog
Explore computer use for a UI-driven task
WEEKS.ai: Use AI to design the decomposition — which capabilities belong in which agent, and what the handoff contract looks like. Reasoning about boundaries out loud is how you get good at this.
WEEKS.checkpoint: Two agents, one MCP tool integration, one working A2A handoff.

WEEKS.title: Agent evaluation & testing
WEEKS.intent: Almost nobody does this part. That is exactly why it differentiates you.
learn: AB-620 domain three: test sets, evaluation methods, Application Insights, solutions and pipelines
build: A test set of 30+ representative utterances with expected outcomes
Run evaluations, review results, iterate on instructions and knowledge
Wire up Application Insights for agent telemetry
Package the agent into a solution with environment variables — no hardcoded values
Deploy DEV to TEST via Power Platform Pipelines
WEEKS.ai: Ask AI for 40 adversarial utterances — ambiguous phrasing, out-of-scope requests, prompt injection attempts, hostile users. Run them. Fix what breaks. This is agent red-teaming, a real skill in short supply.
WEEKS.checkpoint: Evaluation results before and after one iteration cycle, showing measured improvement.

WEEKS.title: ALM, governance & the rebuild
WEEKS.intent: The capstone. Package everything properly and ship it through a pipeline.
learn: ALM for Power Platform, solutions, Power Platform Pipelines
CoE Starter Kit, DLP policies, environment strategy
watch: Search: Power Platform ALM pipelines 2026
Search: Power Platform CoE Starter Kit
build: Package everything as a managed solution with proper publisher and prefix
Externalise every connection reference and environment variable — zero hardcoded values
Full DEV to TEST to PROD deployment via pipelines
Apply a DLP policy and document its impact on your solution
Install the CoE Starter Kit in a sandbox and explore what it surfaces
Write an architecture decision record covering every significant choice across 24 weeks
Sit AB-620 this week or next, depending on how Weeks 22–23 went
WEEKS.ai: Have AI interrogate your architecture decision record — for each decision, ask it to argue the opposing choice. Where you can't defend yourself, you've found a gap.
WEEKS.checkpoint: Deployed to PROD through a pipeline. ADR written. Real users using it.
